malicious_token_can_execute_during_trans.meaning: the token involved in addRewards is malicious and can execute code during transferFrom

accounting_increased_before_transfer.meaning: pending-reward accounting has already been increased at the time the external transferFrom executes

reentry_into_claim_rewards_during_transf.meaning: claimRewards or another entrypoint is re-entered while accounting has already been increased during the addRewards external transferFrom

tokens_stolen_via_combined_weaknesses.meaning: tokens may be stolen by combining the reentrancy weakness with other weaknesses

assumptions: addRewards updates pending-reward accounting before performing the external transferFrom.
The reentrancy window is the interval during the external transferFrom after accounting has been increased.

unresolved.description: Report does not state who calls addRewards or whether the caller is authorized, so the applicability scope of the reentrancy-window requirement cannot be fully bound.
Report does not specify concrete token amounts or numeric bounds for the reentrancy window; the window is represented qualitatively.
Token theft is described as conditional ('may be combined with other weaknesses'); the specific combined weaknesses and extraction path are not defined.

limitations: The selected impact is potential and conditional; the plan does not assert that token theft is inevitable.
The reentrancy window and accounting-increase ordering are represented as grounded Boolean observables rather than numeric amounts.
Other selected intents for this impact, if any, are formalized in separate independent claims and are not combined here.
Runtime binding of the malicious token behavior and entrypoint re-entry is deferred to later stages.
